original_title: Divergent C3–C4 Bond Cleavage of Spiro β-Lactams for the Switchable Synthesis of 3,3-Disubstituted Oxindoles and 2-Arylacrylamides
title: One diazoketone, light, and a fork toward oxindoles or acrylamides
blurb: A visible-light Wolff rearrangement/Staudinger cycloaddition between α-diazoketones and quinone imine ketals builds spiro β-lactams that then cleave at C3–C4 under acid or heat, giving 3,3-disubstituted oxindoles one way and 2-arylacrylamides the other. Metal-free, one pot, only N2 and methanol as byproducts, and the split between concerted and stepwise pathways is apparently what makes the switch work at all.

original_title: Disulfide engineering of the FANCM-MHF complex reveals constraints on crosslink design in symmetric oligomers.
title: Disulfide-locking FANCM-MHF exposes limits on symmetric crosslinking
blurb: Engineered disulfides in the FANCM-MHF complex map where crosslinks can and can't go in a symmetric oligomer, a constraint worth knowing before trying to trap this kind of assembly.

original_title: Toward Chromatography-Free Convergent Peptide Synthesis via Nanostar Sieving
title: Skipping chromatography in peptide synthesis with a nanostar filter
blurb: Organic solvent nanofiltration through an 8-arm, 20 kDa nanostar support keeps a 39-mer peptide soluble up to 40 mM while it's assembled from eight fragments, with the nanofiltration doing the purification job chromatography usually handles. Liquid-phase peptide synthesis without a column.

original_title: Engineering injectable alginate hydrogels for mesenchymal stem cell delivery: comparative evaluation of ionic crosslinking strategies and early in vitro outcomes.
title: Picking an ionic crosslinker for injectable stem-cell hydrogels
blurb: Compares ionic crosslinking strategies for alginate hydrogels meant to deliver mesenchymal stem cells by injection, with results so far limited to early in vitro outcomes.

original_title: Cu(II)-Catalyzed Coupling of Unactivated Alkenes with Sodium Sulfinates for Allylic Sulfones
title: Cu(II) turns unactivated alkenes into allylic sulfones
blurb: A directed copper(II)-catalyzed sulfonylation couples sodium sulfinates with unactivated alkenes, including internal-alkene 3-butenoic acids, to give allylic sulfones with high regioselectivity under simple conditions. Scope covers both aromatic and aliphatic sulfinates, with follow-up derivatization of the sulfone products and control experiments backing the proposed mechanism.

original_title: Simplifying Radical Cross-Coupling by Deleting Redox
title: Radical cross-coupling that skips the redox step
blurb: Radical cross-coupling usually needs an external redox activator bolted on to get going, which adds complexity and caps scalability. This version runs redox-neutral instead, doing the C–C coupling straight off abundant functional groups under mild conditions without that extra machinery.

original_title: Asymmetric Kinetic Resolution of 2‐Aryl Oxetanes by Dinuclear Titanium Radical Catalysis
title: A kinetic resolution for oxetanes nobody had cracked
blurb: A dinuclear salen-titanium catalyst opens 2-aryl oxetanes through a radical mechanism, resolving racemates into enantioenriched product with solid regio- and enantioselectivity. It works across aryl, heteroaryl, and even drug-conjugated substrates, notable mainly because a general kinetic resolution for this strained-ring class basically didn't exist before.

original_title: Sustained-Release GelMA-Quercetin Hydrogel Accelerates Diabetic Foot Ulcer Healing via Foxo3-Mediated Macrophage Autophagy and M2 Polarization.
title: A quercetin hydrogel for diabetic ulcers, mechanism included
blurb: A sustained-release GelMA hydrogel loaded with quercetin speeds diabetic foot ulcer healing, working through Foxo3 to push macrophages toward autophagy and M2 polarization.

original_title: Decoupling the Impact of Surface Functionalization over Pt at the Cathode on Kinetics and Mass Transport in PEMFCs
title: Fixing the Pt-ionomer interface in fuel cells with a spacer molecule
blurb: Nafion's sulfonate groups poison Pt sites at the PEMFC cathode and choke off oxygen transport. This work pre-adsorbs 7-ethyltheophylline onto Pt before the ionomer goes on, an "ETP-first" sequencing that lets them control the interface and tease apart its effect on reaction kinetics from its effect on mass transport.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Harnessing Regiodivergence and Enantioselectivity in Hydroamidation of Methylenecyclopropanes by Ligand Control
title: Ligands decide which end of the methylenecyclopropane gets aminated
blurb: Ni-catalyzed hydroamidation of methylenecyclopropanes with dioxazolones, where the ligand choice flips the reaction between regioisomers and does it enantioselectively. Base-metal-catalyzed remote asymmetric hydroamination of aliphatic olefins has barely been explored, so getting both regiocontrol and ee out of one Ni system is the notable part.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Expanding the Living Polymerization Toolkit: Mechanistic Insights and Optimization of Vinyl-Addition Polymerization of Norbornenes
title: Debugging why norbornene vinyl-addition polymerization stops being living
blurb: A tri-tert-butylphosphine-ligated cationic Pd initiator runs living vinyl-addition polymerization of norbornenes, and this paper works out the mechanism behind the molecular-weight control loss that's plagued the method, then optimizes around it for better MW control.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A Visualizable Injectable Multifunctional Sericin Hydrogel with Facile Fabrication for Versatile Wound Care.
title: An injectable sericin hydrogel you can actually see going in
blurb: A visualizable, injectable sericin hydrogel for wound care, pitched as multifunctional and simple to fabricate.

original_title: CDCP1-targeted antibody-drug conjugates and immunocytokines for cancer therapy.
title: CDCP1 as an antibody-drug conjugate target
blurb: A review covering CDCP1-targeted antibody-drug conjugates and immunocytokines being developed for cancer therapy.

original_title: An Artificial Molecular Transducer Driven by Molecular Recognition
title: A molecular transducer with a cavity that only appears when signaled
blurb: This synthetic system starts with no working binding cavity. An exogenous signaling molecule binds, triggers a conformational change, and only then does a cavity open up for guest recognition. They use photoresponsive anthracene as the signal, making the whole thing an artificial stand-in for how biological signaling molecules gate function.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Amplifying multiplex spatial profiling with tyramide oligonucleotides
title: Stacking tyramide amplification with DNA barcodes for spatial multiplexing
blurb: PASTA conjugates tyramide to oligonucleotides so any assay that reads out through horseradish peroxidase can be amplified and layered with other modalities in the same spatial image, aimed at the usual bottleneck of combining and boosting signals in imaging-based spatial biology.

original_title: Atroposelective Ion-Pair Catalysis: Accessing C−C and C−N Axially Chiral Amino Acid Derivatives from Prochiral Electrophiles
title: A chiral ion pair sets axial stereocenters on the way to amino acid derivatives
blurb: A quinine-derived ammonium catalyst runs a dynamic kinetic resolution on prochiral electrophiles, ring-opening them with alcohols so the axial C–C or C–N stereocenter forms as the bond does. Over 60 examples with yields and ee's both pushing 99%, which is a strong showing if it holds up past the paper's own substrate list.

original_title: Advances in Carbon‐Nitrogen Bond Formation From CO 2 and Nitrogenous Small Molecules Through Tandem Electrocatalysis
title: CO2 electroreduction picks up a nitrogen partner
blurb: A review making the case for coupling CO2 electroreduction with reduction of nitrogen species like N2, nitrate, and nitrite, so the products carry C–N bonds instead of just the usual narrow slate CO2 alone gives you, while cleaning up two waste streams at once. It's a survey, so no new numbers, just the argument for why tandem electrocatalysis is worth the trouble.

original_title: Ce/Zr-MOF- and TCEP-Mediated Ascorbic Acid Generation for In Situ Oxygen Vacancy Regulation in Bi4O5I2/Bi2S3 Gate: A Triple-Mode Biosensor for ALKBH5 Detection
title: Three readouts for one RNA demethylase, off an ascorbic acid trick
blurb: ALKBH5's demethylation activity throttles ascorbic acid generation, built here from TCEP reducing dehydroascorbic acid and a Ce/Zr-MOF hydrolyzing a phosphate precursor, and that ascorbic acid then drives a Bi4O5I2/Bi2S3 gate through photoelectrochemical, OPECT, and colorimetric signals all at once. Convoluted chain of chemistry, but three independent readouts off one sample is a real hedge against a false positive.

original_title: PSMA Radioligand Therapy: Success and Limitations to Date.
title: Where PSMA radioligand therapy actually stands
blurb: A review weighing what PSMA radioligand therapy has actually delivered in the clinic against where it's still falling short.

original_title: Regulating transport processes in oxygen evolution catalyst layers for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis
title: PEM electrolyzers live or die on plumbing, not just catalyst
blurb: A look at transport processes inside the oxygen-evolution catalyst layer of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers, the mass-transport side of the problem rather than the catalyst chemistry itself.

original_title: N -Phenylhydroxylamine-Induced Radical Relay for the Synthesis of α-Trifluoromethyl Ketones
title: A radical relay turns alkynes into α-CF3 ketones
blurb: N-phenylhydroxylamine drives a previously unused radical relay that takes alkynes plus Togni's reagent straight to α-trifluoromethyl ketones, with broad scope and enough functional group tolerance to work late-stage on more complex molecules. New role for a reagent that's usually just sitting around.

original_title: Total Synthesis of (+)-Psychotrimine and Formal Synthesis of (+)-Psychotetramine via Late-Stage Ni(II)-Photoredox N-Arylation
title: Blue LEDs close out the psychotrimine synthesis
blurb: Total synthesis of (+)-psychotrimine and a formal synthesis of (+)-psychotetramine, built by adding indole onto a bromopyrroloindole and then stitching the oligomeric pyrroloindole scaffold together with a late-stage Ni(II)-photoredox C–N coupling under blue LEDs. Saving the hardest bond for a light-driven step at the end, instead of forcing it earlier, is the actual move here.

original_title: Enzyme/Nanozyme Cascade Catalysis-Driven Trimodal Platform Using a Readily Prepared Single-Component Nanozyme for Highly Efficient Metabolic Biomarker Assays
title: One nanozyme, three readouts, for galactose and xanthine oxidase
blurb: A single-component nanozyme, an iron-loaded ZnTcPP MOF, swaps in for the usual multicomponent nanozyme blends and still drives fluorescent, colorimetric, and photothermal readouts off the same cascade, demonstrated on galactose and xanthine oxidase as the metabolic markers. Fewer moving parts for the same trimodal output, assuming sensitivity doesn't take the hit.

original_title: Lewis Acid-Catalyzed ( n + 2) ( n = 5, 6) High-Order Dipolar Annulation of Photogenerated Ketenes: Unified Synthesis of Seven- and Eight-Membered Diazaheterocycles
title: Photogenerated ketenes build the seven- and eight-membered rings that are usually a pain
blurb: Visible light runs a Wolff rearrangement on α-diazoketones to make ketenes in situ, and a Lewis acid then walks them through a (n+2) annulation with imidazolidines or hexahydropyrimidines to build seven- and eight-membered diazaheterocycles, rings that are medicinally relevant but a slog to make directly. One method covering both ring sizes, with mild conditions and broad tolerance by their account.

original_title: Liquid-like Indium Mobility Governs the Activity, Selectivity, and Stability of In2O3–ZrO2/SAPO-34 Catalysts for Syngas-to-Olefin Conversion
title: Indium goes liquid-like inside the catalyst, and that explains everything else
blurb: In2O3–ZrO2/SAPO-34 catalysts for syngas-to-olefin conversion turn out to hinge on indium species moving around like a liquid within the oxide-zeolite composite, and that mobility tracks with activity, selectivity, and how well the catalyst survives hydrogen-rich conditions. They tie it to indium loading, the oxide-to-zeolite ratio, and pretreatment, pinning down the stability question that's been the open issue with this catalyst family.

original_title: High-Temperature CO2 Reduction: Operando Analysis and Reaction Dynamics
title: Operando look at why high-temp CO2 reduction stalls
blurb: They ran RWGS- and SOEC-style high-temperature CO2 conversion under operando conditions to watch the catalyst while it's actually working. The headline problem is the usual one: whatever makes the catalyst active also seems to wear it out, so that activity-stability tradeoff is still what's standing between this and real syngas plants.

original_title: Unlocking Free α-Trifluoromethoxy Carbene Reactivity from Aldehyde
title: Aldehydes turned into a free OCF3 carbene, apparently a first
blurb: Aryl, alkenyl, and alkynyl aldehydes converted into an α-trifluoromethoxy carbene via an isolable or in-situ secondary chloride, something nobody had managed before. OCF3 groups are getting looked at as PFAS stand-ins, so a clean route into that carbene chemistry from ordinary aldehydes is worth watching if it generalizes past the reported substrates.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Radioligand Therapy of the Prostate - the Sky Is the Limit?
title: Prostate radioligand therapy: sky's the limit, or just hype
blurb: A perspective piece asking how far radioligand therapy for prostate cancer can realistically go, not a data paper. Titles that answer their own rhetorical question with 'the sky is the limit' are usually selling something, so I'd want the trial numbers before buying it.

original_title: Tribenzotriquinacene Fused Dimers (“Fusodimers”)—Synthesis and Host–Guest Properties
title: Two triquinacene bowls fused together, only one shape traps fullerenes
blurb: Two tribenzotriquinacene bowls sharing a single benzene ring, made as syn and anti stereoisomers. The biconcave syn version hosts C60 and C70 as 1:1 complexes in both solution and the solid state, but the convex-concave anti isomer doesn't. Same pieces, different geometry, only one of them catches a fullerene.

original_title: PASTA: versatile tyramide-oligonucleotide amplification for multimodal spatial biology
title: One amplification chemistry for every spatial imaging modality
blurb: PASTA is a tyramide-oligonucleotide signal amplification scheme built to be platform-agnostic, so the same boost works across multiplexed imaging modalities instead of needing a bespoke protocol for each. A methods paper, but a useful one if it drops into existing pipelines as easily as advertised.

original_title: Guest-programmed adaptive reconfiguration in heteroleptic metal–organic cages
title: Zn cages that rearrange into other Zn cages on command from the guest
blurb: Heteroleptic pentagonal prismatic ZnII cages, built by matching pentatopic and tetratopic ligand edge lengths, that reconfigure cage-to-cage when guests show up. It's not one guest flipping a switch, it's cooperative multi-guest interactions driving the swap, which is the harder trick in systems this prone to kinetic traps and scrambling.

original_title: Emergence of Nido -Icosahedral Superatomic Units in Iridium-Doped Silver Cluster Assemblies
title: Iridium-doped silver clusters build superatoms out of smaller superatoms
blurb: Three new Ir-doped, silver-rich 16-electron clusters whose cores turn out to be two 8-electron superatomic units fused together, confirmed by single-crystal X-ray. Superatoms assembled from superatoms, and a decent argument that the framework extends past the usual spherical clusters into these nido-icosahedral shapes.

original_title: Lattice Mn Doping Enables Dual-Pathway CO2 Methanation on Ru/Cr2O3
title: A little Mn in the lattice and Ru/Cr2O3 stops needing so much heat for CO2 methanation
blurb: Doping Mn into the Cr2O3 lattice itself, not just the surface, takes Ru/Cr2O3 from 4% CO2 conversion at 200°C to 91% on the optimized Mn0.10Cr0.90Ox version, with a 4.1x jump in turnover. Lattice doping beating surface modification is the actual finding, and it's a big enough jump that low-temperature methanation looks a lot less like a compromise.

original_title: Thio-Mannich-Type Reactions for C-H Thioalkylation of Carbon Nucleophiles
title: Swap the amine for a thiol and the Mannich reaction does C-H thioalkylation
blurb: A thio-Mannich variant that uses a thiol nucleophile in place of the amine, reacting aldehydes with carbon nucleophiles like methyl ketones or enones to install thioalkyl groups directly. Nobody had closed this loop before, despite the Mannich reaction being about as classic as multicomponent reactions get.

original_title: Enthalpy‐Entropy Molecular Design of Gel Polymer Electrolytes for Regulating Solvation Chemistry in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
title: Tuning enthalpy and entropy separately to fix lithium-sulfur's gel electrolyte problem
blurb: Li-S gel polymer electrolytes are held back by two things at once: Li+ desolvation costs too much enthalpy, and polysulfide conversion is too slow. This design treats both as one solvation-structure problem, engineering enthalpy and entropy together to restrict which reaction pathways are available while also controlling how polysulfides coordinate in the gel.

original_title: Numerical simulation-guided development of dynamic kinetic resolution reactions
title: The number to actually watch in dynamic kinetic resolution
blurb: DKR's measured ee depends on both catalyst stereoselectivity and reaction conditions, which is exactly the problem: pseudo-selectivity muddies any attempt to judge the catalyst on its own. Simulations show the initial ee, measured in a low-conversion window, tracks catalyst stereoselectivity almost independent of conditions, so that's the number worth optimizing against instead of the endpoint value everyone reports.

original_title: Virus-like particles enable targeted gene engineering and pooled CRISPR screening in primary human myeloid cells
title: VLPs get CRISPR screening working in primary human myeloid cells
blurb: Myeloid cells are a pain to edit efficiently, but virus-like particles deliver the editing machinery well enough to run pooled CRISPR screens directly in primary human myeloid cells, not a cell line standing in for them.

original_title: Synthesis of Hexagonal CaB3C3 with a Zeolite-Type Framework
title: A zeolite framework built from boron and carbon instead of oxygen
blurb: Calcium-intercalated CaB3C3 crystallizes in the zeolite NPO topology under high pressure and high temperature, four-coordinate B/C channels forming the same kind of ion-trapping structure predicted for some hypothetical metastable carbon allotropes, and with barely any framework disorder. DFT calculations then check whether it's genuinely thermodynamically stable or just parked there by the synthesis conditions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Water Structure within Ternary Solvents Suggests Nanophase Formation
title: Oil dropped into water/cosolvent mixtures reorganizes the water lattice
blurb: Raman spectroscopy with multivariate curve resolution tracks how water's hydrogen-bonding network shifts in ternary mixtures of water, a cosolvent (acetone, DMF, or DMSO), and an oil (2-hexanone or 2-pentanone) as the oil gets added. The pattern points to nanophase formation rather than a smoothly blended mixture.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Revealing Excited-State Electrochemical Reaction Pathways at Solid Electrolyte Interphases by Ab Initio Nonadiabatic Molecular Dynamics
title: What an SEI electron does in the femtoseconds after it lands
blurb: Most electrochemical frameworks only track equilibrium energetics and skip what an injected electron actually does right after transfer. Ab initio nonadiabatic molecular dynamics follows the excited-state pathways at the solid electrolyte interphase instead, catching nonequilibrium reactivity the equilibrium picture just doesn't see.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Tensile Expansion Mass Spectrometry for single cell metabolomics imaging
title: Single-cell metabolomics imaging without the custom rig
blurb: MALDI imaging maps biomolecules across tissue but usually can't hit single-cell resolution without bespoke instrumentation and real expertise. Tensile expansion mass spectrometry is pitched as a way to get single-cell metabolic imaging working for people who don't want to build their own setup to do it.

original_title: Frontispiece: Probing Into Asymmetric Dearomatizing Photocycloadditions of 2‐Naphthalene Derivatives With Alkenes: [2 + 2] and [4 + 2] Pathways
title: Naphthalenes go dearomatized two different ways under light
blurb: Asymmetric photocycloadditions send 2-naphthalene derivatives reacting with alkenes down either a [2+2] or a [4+2] path, dearomatizing the ring on the way, with which pathway wins as the real question the piece is probing.

original_title: Nanoparticle Conversion Chemistry: A Synthetic Framework for Multielemental Nanostructures
title: A framework for turning simple nanoparticles into multielemental ones
blurb: Solution-phase synthesis has mono- and bimetallic nanoparticle control down, but adding more elements usually breaks because every precursor brings its own solubility and redox quirks. This lays out a synthetic framework, built around converting nanoparticles stepwise, for getting multielemental nanostructures under control instead of tuning each recipe by trial and error.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Shortwave-Infrared (SWIR) Tetrabenzannulated Silicon-Rhodamine
title: A rhodamine dye pushed out past 1000 nm for SWIR imaging
blurb: Good SWIR dyes (1000 nm and beyond, bright and stable enough for in vivo use) are still in short supply, and there's no real standard for evaluating them either. ESi7 is a tetrabenzannulated silicon-rhodamine built on three deliberate moves, benzannulation for the red shift, steric shielding for stability, deep rigidification for brightness, made via a convergent synthesis.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Multitarget Molecular Imaging-based Characterization of Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor.
title: Reading GI stromal tumors with more than one imaging target
blurb: A clinical nuclear medicine report on characterizing gastrointestinal stromal tumors using multitarget molecular imaging.

original_title: The Catalytic Asymmetric Alkylation of Olefins with Alcohol Derivatives
title: Friedel-Crafts-style alkylation, but for olefins instead of arenes
blurb: Arene alkylation with electrophiles is old news, but doing it to unactivated olefins wasn't really a thing. This one runs asymmetric benzylation and allylation off acetate leaving groups using a single imidodiphosphorimidate catalyst acting as a silylium Lewis acid. The mechanism goes through an SN1 ion pair that erases the stereochemical info entirely, and the catalyst still steers it back to one enantiomer on the way out.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Accelerated Deprotonation Triggered by the Se–Ru–O Asymmetric Configuration Enables Acidic Oxygen Evolution
title: Doping selenium into RuO2 so it stops falling apart in acid
blurb: RuO2 is already the benchmark acidic OER catalyst; its usual problems are degradation and sluggish proton-coupled electron transfer. Se doping breaks the local symmetry into a Se-Ru-O motif that speeds up deprotonation, and the paper reports gains in both activity and stability at once, which is the combination everyone wants and rarely actually gets.

original_title: Dehydrogenative Access to Aluminyl Metalloligands
title: Stripping hydrogens off an aluminum hydride to make it a ligand
blurb: Dihydridoaluminates are normally just hydride donors, but one built on a dipyrromethene-diphosphine scaffold gets dehydrogenated with H2 release when it meets group 10 metal precursors, landing as clean Al(I)-M(II) complexes. Swap in Ni(0) instead and it only half-dehydrogenates, kicking out LiH and leaving hydride-bridged Al-Ni clusters. Same starting material, different metal, different outcome.

original_title: A Crystallographic Descriptor for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution on Nickel
title: Mapping which nickel grains actually do the hydrogen evolution work
blurb: Polycrystalline Ni is what you'd actually use, not a single crystal, but nobody had a real descriptor tying grain orientation to alkaline HER activity. Combining scanning electrochemical cell microscopy with EBSD on the same spots gives grain-resolved activity across 52 grains, and it varies a lot by orientation. A pseudo-single-crystal dataset built the hard way instead of assumed.

original_title: The Dual Role of DNA Cross-linking Agents: From Genotoxicity to cGAS-STING-Mediated Immune Activation.
title: DNA-damaging drugs might also be quietly switching on cGAS-STING
blurb: Cross-linking agents get framed almost entirely as genotoxic. This flags the other side, that the DNA damage they cause can also trip cGAS-STING immune signaling, linking a mutagenic mechanism to an immune-activating one.

original_title: Phenonium-Ion-Mediated Skeletal Editing of Paracyclophanes
title: Reviving phenonium ions to edit paracyclophane skeletons
blurb: Phenonium ions have been a physical-organic curiosity for decades, rarely a synthesis tool. Here a one-carbon handle gets bolted onto the aliphatic bridge of a paracyclophane, BF3 activates the alcohol under conditions that dodge plain solvolysis, and the resulting phenonium ion opens regioselectively with external nucleophiles. The payoff is modular access to bigger paracyclophane homologs from a textbook cation nobody had put to work this way.

original_title: Living circuit boards built by printing bacterial transistors
title: Printing bacteria in patterns that compute like a circuit board
blurb: Regular circuit boards get their function from how components are arranged. This does the equivalent with bacteria, printing different strains in specific spatial layouts on a surface so the arrangement itself, not just each strain's individual behavior, is what computes the output.

original_title: Few‐Layer MoS 2 –Decorated MoO 2 for High‐Density Exposed Catalytic Heterointerfaces in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
title: A battery separator coating that both traps and converts polysulfides
blurb: Li-S batteries lose capacity to polysulfides wandering off and to slow sulfur redox. This separator coating pairs few-layer MoS2 with MoO2 on carbon nanotubes, so the polar MoO2 anchors the polysulfides while the MoS2 handles catalyzing their conversion, at a high density of exposed heterointerfaces where the two actually meet.

original_title: Development and Applications of Biosensors Integrating Molecularly Imprinted Polymers and Aptamers for Life Sciences and Healthcare
title: Pairing molecularly imprinted polymers with aptamers in one biosensor
blurb: A rundown of biosensors combining molecularly imprinted polymers, synthetic plastic receptors standing in for antibodies, with aptamers for life-science and healthcare sensing. A survey of where that pairing stands rather than one new device.

original_title: Nanoconfined supersaturated reactors for efficient CO<sub>2</sub>-to-ethanol electroreduction
title: Squeezing extra CO2 into the reaction zone to push past ethylene to ethanol
blurb: Copper CO2 reduction usually struggles to go selectively past two-carbon products. This nanoconfined reactor locally supersaturates CO2 right at the catalyst, which stabilizes ethoxy intermediates and gets ethanol to 70.3% Faradaic efficiency at current densities that are actually usable, not just lab-toy currents.

original_title: Bridgehead-Functionalized Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes – Promising Saturated Isosteres of Monosubstituted Benzene
title: A saturated stand-in for plain phenyl, now actually scalable
blurb: Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes already cover ortho- and meta-disubstituted benzene mimicry, but the bridgehead-monofunctionalized version, the direct swap for a monosubstituted phenyl ring, has been basically unobtainable. This paper works out two separate routes to the key bridgehead carboxylic acid and maps where the core sits on the bicycloalkane physicochemical scale. A building block paper, but a gap that's been sitting open a while.

original_title: Heterobimetallic Janus Catalysts for the One‐Pot Synthesis of Polar‐Apolar Block Copolymers
title: One catalyst, two incompatible polymerizations, one pot
blurb: A heterobimetallic Janus catalyst runs olefin polymerization and lactone ring-opening in the same flask to build polyolefin-polyester block copolymers directly, instead of the usual multi-catalyst, multi-step, isolate-and-purify slog. The two mechanisms don't normally play nice together, so getting them to cooperate without stepping on each other is the actual trick here.

original_title: Recent Advances in the Synthesis of Citronellal from Citral
title: Citronellal from citral, the industrial cheat sheet
blurb: A review, not new chemistry: rounds up how citral gets converted to citronellal, the mint-derived precursor to menthol and citronellol, with asymmetric hydrogenation still the go-to for enantioselectivity. Handy if you want the industrial process landscape in one place, not if you're after a new reaction.

original_title: AI-Assisted SERS Decoding of Dual Enzymatic Activity for Intraoperative Chemical Mapping of Epilepsy
title: SERS plus AI to map a seizure focus while you're still cutting
blurb: An AI-accelerated SERS platform tracks caspase-3 and MMP-2 activity at once to mark epileptic foci during surgery, with an AI-selected MMP-2 peptide substrate fixing the kinetic mismatch that normally makes dual-enzyme tracking fall apart. The pitch is real-time molecular guidance for resection margins instead of eyeballing it, though it's a proof-of-concept platform, not something in an OR yet.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
